title: Trading Policy

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: A person having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the Company's activities (including any Director, Key Management Personnel), a Senior Employee, a Key Consultant or Key Contractor, and any Connected Person of those persons. All substantive dealing rules (Prohibited Periods, no short-term trading, no placing of orders, prior approval) apply uniformly to this tier; only the approver differs by sub-category.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Restricted Persons who are Directors; distinguished only for approval (Chairman or the Board; the Chairman requires Board approval) and ASX notification of dealings.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Restricted Persons with authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the Company's activities, excluding Directors; distinguished only for approval (Managing Director).

tiers.name: Senior Employee, Key Consultant or Key Contractor
tiers.description: Senior employees and key consultants/contractors engaged by the Group; distinguished only for approval (Company Secretary).

tiers.name: Connected Person
tiers.description: Spouse or partner, child or step-child under 18, a parent, an unlisted body corporate controlled by or of which the Restricted Person is a director, a trust of which the Restricted Person is trustee and beneficiary (or a related person is beneficiary), or any other person over whom the Restricted Person has significant influence or control. Deemed a Restricted Person themselves; the Restricted Person must perform the relevant obligations in respect of the Connected Person.

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to release of the Company's full year results
windows.end_anchor: two days after release of the Company's full year results

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to release of the Company's half year results
windows.end_anchor: two days after release of the Company's half year results

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may impose an Additional Period from time to time, for example because the Company is considering matters that would require disclosure to the market but for Listing Rule 3.1A. Confidentiality of an Additional Period is not addressed.

rules.detail: Company Securities is defined to expressly include derivatives 'of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise', so an OTC put/call is squarely a Company Security. Dealing in it requires the same prior approval, avoidance of Inside Information and Prohibited Period compliance as an ordinary share trade; the Policy draws no distinction by vesting state.
rules.evidence: derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise

rules.detail: 'Hedges' is listed only as an example of a derivative Company Security; there is no dedicated hedging clause, prohibition, or hedging-specific approval process. A hedge is therefore governed by the same general approval/blackout regime as any other dealing.
rules.evidence: derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options)

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar structure would be a derivative Company Security (buying or selling a financial product settled in cash or otherwise), caught only through the Company Securities/dealing definitions and so subject to ordinary prior approval and blackout rules.
rules.evidence: derivatives of any of the above ... whether settled by cash or otherwise

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the Policy.
Securities lending is not named anywhere in the Policy.

CFDs are not named specifically, but would fall within 'derivatives ... whether settled by cash or otherwise' and so require ordinary prior approval; a short CFD position would also engage the no short-term trading guidance in 4.2.
rules.evidence: derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise

rules.detail: Margin lending against Company Securities is expressly contemplated, not prohibited: a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights 'for example, under a margin lending arrangement' is a standing exception, and funding an option exercise price with a margin loan is discussed only in terms of the resale risk it creates, not banned.
rules.evidence: dispose of Company Securities resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

rules.detail: Providing Company Securities to a lender as security 'by way of mortgage or charge' is expressly acknowledged as something that can occur, and a sale on default under that mortgage or charge is stated not to breach insider trading laws. Creating the encumbrance itself is not listed as a regulated dealing requiring approval.
rules.evidence: Where Company Securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.

rules.detail: No prohibition on secured financing of any kind against Company Securities; margin loans, mortgages and charges are all expressly discussed as legitimate arrangements that can lawfully result in a lender-driven sale, including via the standing exception in 4.5(a)(xii).
rules.evidence: where the exercise price of options is being provided by a margin loan or other form of lending arrangement then there may be a risk that the Restricted Person may need to sell shares to avoid providing additional capital or security to the lender in the event of a decrease in the value of the shares.

rules.detail: Guideline-strength prohibition ('should never') on short-term trading, with no defined holding period, carved out for option exercises followed by a prompt sale.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons should never engage in short-term trading of Company Securities except for the exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter.

clearance.approver: Chairman or the Board (Board approves the Chairman)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: promptly, to enable ASX notification within 5 business days
clearance.evidence: Any director wishing to buy, sell or exercise rights in relation to Company Securities must obtain the prior approval of the Chairman or the Board before doing so.
Any Key Management Personnel wishing to buy, sell or exercise rights in relation to Company Securities must obtain the prior approval of the Managing Director before doing so.

clearance.tier: Senior Employee, Key Consultant or Key Contractor
clearance.evidence: Any Senior Employee, Key Consultant or Key Contractor wishing to buy, sell or exercise rights in relation to Company Securities must obtain the prior approval of the Company Secretary before doing so.

clearance.approver: Managing Director (Senior Employees/Consultants/Contractors), Chairman (Directors) or the Board (Chairman), per 5.5
clearance.evidence: A Restricted Person who is not in possession of Inside Information ... may be given prior written clearance ... to sell or otherwise dispose of Company Securities during a Prohibited Period where the person is in severe financial hardship or where there are exceptional circumstances ... Any exemption, if issued, will be in writing and shall contain a specified time period during which the sale of Company Securities can be made.

carve_outs: exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter
short_term.evidence: Restricted Persons should never engage in short-term trading of Company Securities except for the exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter.

exceptions.evidence: Restricted Persons may be in severe financial hardship if they have a pressing financial commitment that can not be satisfied other than by selling Company Securities.

Exceptional circumstances may apply to the disposal of Company Securities by a Restricted Person if the person is required by a court order, a court enforceable undertaking for example in a bona fide family settlement, to transfer or sell Company Securities or there is some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement to do so.
dispose of Company Securities resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

make an investment in, or trade in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the securities of the Company) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party.
trade under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with procedures set out in this policy.
undertake to accept, or accept, a takeover offer.

trade under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board.

exercise (but not sell securities following exercise) an option or a right under an employee incentive scheme, or convert a convertible security, where the final date for the exercise ... falls during a Prohibited Period and the Company has been in an exceptionally long Prohibited Period ... and the Restricted Person could not reasonably have been expected to exercise it at a time when free to do so.

where a Restricted Person is a trustee, trade in Company Securities by that trust provided the Restricted Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a Prohibited Period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the Restricted Person.
acquire Company Securities under a dividend reinvestment, or top-up plan that is available to all holders or securities of the same class.
acquire ordinary shares in the Company as a result of the exercise of options held under an employee option scheme.
transfer securities of the Company already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Restricted Person is a beneficiary.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: Where a margin loan or other lending arrangement funds an option exercise price, the Policy flags a risk that the Restricted Person may need to sell shares to avoid providing additional capital or security to the lender if the share value decreases.

exemption_authority: Managing Director (for Senior Employees, Key Consultants or Key Contractors), Chairman (for Directors) or the Board (for the Chairman) may grant a written exemption to sell during a Prohibited Period for severe financial hardship or exceptional circumstances (court order or overriding legal/regulatory requirement), for a specified time period, provided the applicant is not in possession of Inside Information.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where Company Securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike policies that treat a secured lender's enforcement sale as a serious breach, this Policy expressly treats it as lawful and excepted at any time, including in a Prohibited Period, which materially de-risks the bank's enforcement mechanics under a funded collar.

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin loan funding of option exercise
bespoke_clauses.clause: where the exercise price of options is being provided by a margin loan or other form of lending arrangement then there may be a risk that the Restricted Person may need to sell shares to avoid providing additional capital or security to the lender in the event of a decrease in the value of the shares.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Board evidently tolerates debt-funded, share-secured arrangements involving Company Securities generally, supporting the view that a bank loan secured on collared vested shares is not itself objectionable under this Policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The placing of orders is prohibited. Restricted Persons must accept the bid or the asking price matching the available number of shares that are bid or offered when trading in the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This on-market execution constraint should not apply to a privately negotiated OTC collar with a bank, but would constrain any on-market delta-hedge or true-up trade the Restricted Person executes personally.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy does not distinguish unvested, vested-but-locked, or vested-unrestricted Company Securities anywhere in the operative dealing rules.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no express carve-out barring a collar or security interest over unvested performance rights/shares, though in practice a lender would still require vested, unencumbered shares capable of being charged.

summary: A funded collar is comparatively achievable under this Policy. Company Securities expressly includes OTC and exchange-traded derivatives, so the put/call legs are dealings requiring the ordinary prior written approval (Chairman/Board for Directors, Managing Director for other KMP, Company Secretary for Senior Employees/Consultants/Contractors), avoidance of Inside Information, and compliance with the two Blackout Periods and any Board-imposed Additional Period; no vesting-state carve-out applies. Critically, the loan leg is not prohibited: margin lending and providing Company Securities as security by mortgage or charge are expressly contemplated, and a lender's forced sale on default or margin call is a standing exception available 'at any time', including during a Prohibited Period, without needing fresh clearance. There is no minimum shareholding requirement, financing disclosure regime, or ban on secured financing to negotiate around. The main residual constraints are the guideline-strength ban on short-term trading (no fixed period) and the general insider trading law, which continues to apply even where clearance has been granted. Overall, subject to ordinary approval and blackout timing, a funded collar secured on vested shares appears structurally permitted.
